title: EXP-036-R2 — Clean Replay: Single Button Name/Caption Recovery Across Designer Save and Form Close/Reopen
objective: Using the existing operator-authenticated Mongoose environment, create exactly one new User-scoped classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_SingleButtonLab02. After confirming its initial clean state and empty component baseline, place exactly one native Toolbox Button, assign Name=FX_SingleButton02 for identity, and set its single tested non-identity property Caption to 'Factory Test Button'. Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after the component configuration and verify the Designer returns clean. Close the target Form using its ordinary Form-tab close control, then reopen exactly the same User-scoped Form through a supported Designer Form-selection or recent-forms path. Verify that exactly one Button with the same Name, Type, and Caption is recovered. Record decisive rendered and property-grid evidence. Limit the conclusion to component-definition recovery across this Save and ordinary close/reopen sequence; do not infer Forms-database durability, cache eviction, or server-side serialization.

in_scope: Review EXP-002-R2, EXP-003-R2, EXP-019-R2, EXP-027, EXP-033-R4, EXP-035-R2, EXP-036 (record and evidence), and the existing verified Form/component recipes before browser mutation.
Repository-only prerequisite review as the first worker task, followed by browser preflight in a separate task.

Standard procedure learned in EXP-036 (no separate authorization needed; record each use): (a) Tabs: the Web Designer opens in its own tab and Chrome does not render background tabs; select the tab you act on, then take a fresh snapshot.

(b) Save Template on wizard page 2: uncheck it by clicking its visible label text once, then verify the checkbox reads unchecked (aria-checked=false); only if still checked, focus it and press Space once; if still checked, stop without Finish.

(c) Component placement: arm the Toolbox Button, then place it with exactly one native coordinate click (browser_mouse_click_xy) on an empty point inside the visible form grid chosen from a fresh screenshot of the selected Designer tab; verify exactly one Button exists before continuing; never repeat the click if the result is ambiguous.

(d) Caption: open the Caption value cell inline editor (double-click the value cell, not the ... picker); if the string-resource list drops down, select nothing from it; enter the literal caption and press Enter; verify the property grid shows it and no resource was chosen.
(e) Scope evidence: the Designer footer shows [ ScopeType: User / ScopeName: <user> ]; use it as visible scope evidence.

(f) Type: the component type is read from the Properties header '<Name> (Button)'; the property-grid row named Type is the button style (PushButton by default) and is recorded, not treated as a mismatch.
Verify the existing Mongoose session is usable, no sign-in or configuration-selection prompt is present, and the intended Web Designer is available in User editing scope.

Use an existing usable Web Designer when present. If absent, permit one ordinary supported Designer launch from the unobstructed Web Client. Require the actual Designer page and User scope to be visible before proceeding.
Confirm FX_SingleButtonLab02 is absent using a supported Select Form workflow with an observable positive control. Do not create the Form if identity or inventory results are ambiguous.
Create exactly one new Form named FX_SingleButtonLab02 using Category Classic, Wizard BuildFromScratch, and the verified basic-Form procedure, with Save Template unchecked.
Verify the created Form's Name, ScopeType=User, ScopeName, clean Designer state, and empty component baseline before adding the Button.
Place exactly one ordinary native Button from the Web Designer Toolbox.
Set Button Name to FX_SingleButton02 as its identity and Caption to exactly Factory Test Button as the sole tested non-identity property.
Capture the selected Button's property grid and rendered Form layout before Save, visibly showing component Type, Name, Caption, and the target Form identity.
Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after configuring the Button and verify Save returns to a clean state without errors.
Reinspect the saved Button and verify its Name, Type, and Caption before closing.
Close exactly the target Form through its ordinary Designer Form-tab close control, without closing the Designer client.
Reopen the exact same User-scoped Form through an already-supported Designer Form-selection path, without cold URL navigation or an unload operation.
Reinspect the reopened component and verify exactly one matching Button, Name=FX_SingleButton02, Type=Button, and Caption=Factory Test Button.
Capture before-Save, after-Save, after-close, and post-reopen screenshots and accessibility/property-grid observations with concise evidence summaries.
Use planned evidence captures for each milestone. Allow at most one additional fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection for ambiguity recovery across the entire experiment.
Write repository documentation only to experiments/EXP-036-R2-clean-replay-single-button-caption-recovery.md and evidence/EXP-036-R2/.
Perform a final read-only audit of the target's recovered state, lifecycle action counts, and repository confinement.

acceptance_checks.description: Repository-review evidence identifies the relevant verified recipes and predecessor experiments before browser mutation. Browser preflight independently shows a usable Mongoose session, a functioning Designer in User editing scope, and no visible unsaved changes or session-establishment prompts. Capture the scope and inherited state. If prerequisites cannot be established, stop without mutation.

Before creation, supported Select Form evidence establishes zero exact and case-insensitive matches for FX_SingleButtonLab02, with a known-existing positive-control row confirming the filter works. The selected Name filter and visible result state must be recorded. Zero visible matches establish absence from the observed Select Form list only: hidden Forms can be excluded by the Show All Forms in Forms List preference, so do not claim that no version of the Form exists anywhere.

Exactly one classic BuildFromScratch Form FX_SingleButtonLab02 is created in User scope. A rendered Designer capture identifies the Form Name, visibly shows User editing scope and a clean Form. Record ScopeType and ScopeName where the rendered UI exposes them; if it does not, record that limitation explicitly instead of failing the check. A component baseline establishes no pre-existing Button or other placed component in the target.

Before Save, rendered Form and component-property evidence shows exactly one newly placed native Button, with Type=Button, Name=FX_SingleButton02, and Caption=Factory Test Button. No additional component placement or unrelated property change is recorded.

Before the Save, commit the Caption edit by moving focus out of the property field through an ordinary supported action (for example Tab or selecting another property row) and confirm the property grid shows the committed value; a displayed value that is still being edited does not prove commitment. Exactly one ordinary Designer Save occurs after the Button configuration. The Designer returns to a visibly clean state, and a post-Save property-grid observation still shows Type=Button, Name=FX_SingleButton02, and Caption=Factory Test Button. Save action and result are recorded.

Exactly one ordinary Form-tab close removes FX_SingleButtonLab02 from the Designer without an unsaved-change prompt. The Designer remains usable. Evidence identifies the target immediately before closure and shows it absent from the open Form tabs afterward. If an unsaved-changes prompt appears after the clean Save, do not answer it (neither discard nor save): capture it and stop blocked.

Exactly one ordinary supported reopen loads FX_SingleButtonLab02. Captured evidence identifies the same Name and visibly User editing scope as before closure, plus ScopeType and ScopeName where the rendered UI exposes them (recording the limitation if it does not). The reopened Designer is visibly clean, and no Save, Regenerate, or unload action occurs during reopening.

Post-reopen rendered evidence and the selected component property grid show exactly one native Button named FX_SingleButton02 with Type=Button and Caption=Factory Test Button. These values match the captured pre-Save and post-Save values, with no duplicate target Button. Classify the result as observed component-definition recovery across ordinary close/reopen only.

The final action and repository audit records one Form creation, one Button placement, one post-configuration Save, one target Form close, and one target Form reopen. Evidence establishes no additional component, prohibited Mongoose mutation, deliberate reauthentication, preference change, or unload action. Worker-authored repository writes are confined to the EXP-036-R2 record and evidence directory, with automatically generated tool artifacts disclosed separately. Record recovery allowance usage and preserve limitations.
